subject: Lumina Health - availability matrix, maintenance carveouts & exception routing
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Beth Andrews <beth.andrews@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Sep 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Lumina Health - availability matrix, maintenance carveouts & exception routing

Hi Beth / Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is our initial redline of the Order Form + SLA language so legal and procurement can see the guardrails we typically ship with for Dedicated/Private customers. High level items we redlined that I want to call out up front: 

- Uptime targets: we proposed an availability banding model (99.95% / 99.9% / 99.5%) with scaled service credits rather than a single hard floor. This helps balance sustained economics for long-running inference workloads.
- Credit caps: a rolling quarterly cap (10% of quarterly committed spend) and single-incident cap (3% per incident) to keep credits bounded.
- Maintenance carveouts: we redlined an explicit emergency maintenance carveout (for P0 hotfixes) plus a 48-hour scheduled maintenance window notice and a yearly blackout cap.
- Response ladder: SLOs for P1/P2/P3 inbound tickets and on-call escalation path (engineering on-call -> ops -> CSM -> account exec).
- Evidence: we linked to SOC 2 and audit logs notes and offered a short ops packet rather than exposing raw logs.

Please review the attached Lumina_OrderForm_SLA_Redline.docx — the redlines include alternative phrasing in the comment stream where we think there is room to compromise (e.g., tightening maintenance notice windows vs. lowering credit caps).

Two asks from our side to move this quickly: 
1) Can you confirm internal Lumina reviewers (legal/procurement/engineering) and their timelines?
2) Are there any required notice periods or procurement rules (e.g., minimum contract amendment lead time) that we should factor into the MAP?

I can loop in our legal lead (Lauren) and ops (Neha) to do a line-by-line call next week if that helps. If yes, propose Tue 9/10 at 10am PT.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137

Subject: Re: Lumina Health - availability matrix, maintenance carveouts & exception routing

Sergio —

Thank you for the redline and the clear summary. A few initial items from Lumina legal/procurement: 

- Maintenance window notice: we cannot accept 48 hours for planned maintenance across the board. For healthcare-critical endpoints we need 7 days notice except for critical security patches. Can you confirm whether you can make a distinction between 'security-critical' and 'standard' maintenance in the language?
- Credit cap: a quarterly cap is acceptable but we need a lower single-incident cap (1.5%) given our regulatory risk profile.
- Uptime bands: we prefer a single minimum availability of 99.95% for production APIs used in patient workflows — tiered bands add negotiation complexity on our side.
- Evidence/Logs: we appreciate the SOC 2 pointer; however, for incident investigations we will need a timelined packet (timestamped request/response traces) for up to 90 days. Please confirm retention windows.

Can Lauren and Neha comment on the operations availability and retention ask? We have procurement deadlines on 9/20 and would like to keep this moving. Happy to take the line-by-line tomorrow afternoon.

Regards,
Beth Andrews
Head of Procurement, Lumina Health
beth.andrews@luminahealth.com | +1 617-555-0194

Beth / Sergio —

Thanks — I reviewed the redline and Beth's asks. For context I lead commercial legal here; below are practical compromise positions that keep Lumina covered while allowing Redwood operational flexibility. I'm proposing colored language you can accept/track in the attached docx. 

Key compromises we can offer: 
1) Maintenance notice: we can scope maintenance notice to 'standard maintenance' (non-security, non-P0) with a 7-day notice for tagged production endpoints and 48-hour notice for non-prod. For emergency security or P0 hotfixes we will provide as much notice as possible and a post-facto incident summary.
2) Uptime: for public production endpoints tied to patient workflows we will lock to 99.95% (as requested). For auxiliary endpoints (batch ingestion, analytics) we keep tiered bands. We can add a definition section to enumerate 'production endpoints' so this is objective.
3) Credit caps: we can accept a lower single-incident cap of 2% (midpoint between 1.5% and 3%) and preserve the quarterly cap at 8% of committed spend. We will also add a carveout to prevent double-crediting for overlapping incidents.
4) Evidence & retention: Redwood retains telemetry and request traces for 180 days by default; we will provide a time-bound incident packet within 5 business days of a validated incident request. If longer retention is needed, we can include an add-on retention service or reference your EDP.

Operational asks of Lumina: please indicate which endpoints you consider 'production' in the MAP (this allows us to auto-classify and reduce disputes on which availability band applies).

Next steps: Sergio and I can host a 45-minute call to run through the doc and mark agreed paragraphs (I suggest Tue 9/10 10am PT per Sergio). If we get alignment on maintenance notice and evidence windows on that call we can produce a clean Order Form for signature before your 9/20 deadline.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0024
